01 — Overview

The situation

SolidRock Building Supplies is a building materials distributor selling cement, rebar, and construction supplies to contractors and developers across Nigeria. They process both cash and credit sales, purchase inventory from suppliers, and manage daily operational expenses.

The Problem

Management had zero real-time visibility into revenue, profitability, or cash flow. Every transaction was manual, every report was guesswork, and customer credit balances were impossible to track reliably.

The Objective

Implement a structured accounting system using Zoho Books to replace manual tracking — covering sales, purchases, inventory, tax compliance, receivables, and bank reconciliation.

Before implementation — the pain points

Sales and expenses recorded manually in spreadsheets — error-prone and time-consuming
Customer credit balances nearly impossible to track across multiple transactions
Supplier payments disorganized — no structured payables system
Financial reports unavailable for real-time decision-making
Bank transactions never regularly reconciled with accounting records

04 — Receivables & Credit Management

Accounts Receivable Aging & Credit Notes

An AR Aging Report was configured to monitor unpaid invoices categorized by how long they've been outstanding — giving management a clear view of who owes what and when it became overdue.

Credit Note — CN-00001 (City Developers ₦48,375 overcharge)

A credit note was issued to correct a billing error — City Developers reported an overcharge of ₦45,000 on a December invoice. The credit note was created and applied to their outstanding balance, correcting both the AR balance and the revenue record.

06 — Tax & Inventory

VAT configuration & inventory tracking

VAT was configured at 7.5% in compliance with Nigerian Federal Inland Revenue Service requirements. VAT collected from customers becomes VAT Payable; VAT paid on purchases becomes Input VAT.

Output VAT − Input VAT
= Net amount owed to FIRS

Inventory tracking was enabled using the FIFO (First In, First Out) method for items like cement and rebar. Example transaction:

Purchase: 100 bags cement @ ₦5,500
Debit Inventory
Sale: 40 bags @ ₦7,200
Credit Inventory

COGS calculated automatically — accurate margin tracking per product line.

VAT Configuration — 7.5% Nigerian Rate
Active Inventory Items — Cement, Rebar, Roofing, Cable
07 — Banking & Reconciliation

Bank reconciliation & daily workflow

A GTBank Current Account was connected and monthly reconciliation performed to ensure accounting records matched bank statements. January 2026 ending balance reconciled: ₦3,366,275.

Banking Overview — GTBank Current + Petty Cash + Undeposited Funds

Daily operational workflow designed for the office manager

01
Record Sales
Create Invoice (credit sale) or Sales Receipt (cash sale) immediately after transaction.
02
Record Customer Payments
Apply payments received against open invoices — updates AR balance automatically.
03
Record Supplier Bills
Enter bills from suppliers with payment terms — tracks AP and upcoming payment obligations.
04
Record Operational Expenses
Rent, salaries, delivery costs, bank charges — all categorized and attached with receipts.
05
End-of-Day Checks
Sales summary, bank balance, and AR report reviewed daily to keep records current and accurate.
08 — Results

What SolidRock achieved

Organized, structured tracking of all sales and purchases — no more spreadsheets
Real-time visibility into customer credit balances and overdue accounts
Accurate VAT calculation and compliance with Nigerian FIRS requirements
Live financial reporting available on demand for management decisions
Reliable monthly bank reconciliation — errors caught before they compound
Automated COGS and inventory valuation using FIFO — accurate margin tracking
